name: Just be rich theory

lead: Just be rich theory (JBR) is a forum idea that money overrides genetics: a wealthy man, proponents say, can buy better grooming, fitness, dental work, clothing, hair restoration and surgery, and also carries status that others find attractive.

It is discussed on looksmax.org as a path to improving one's position without a naturally favoured face. Related academic literature treats status and resources as attractiveness cues, though the theory itself has not been tested as such.

paras: In forum framing, the theory points toward career and income as a long-term route to better looks: funding skincare, cosmetic procedures, personal training and a stronger wardrobe, and gaining the social standing that makes others rate someone higher.

No physical risks attach to the idea itself. Critics inside and outside the community describe it as a slow route that depends on income, and posters disagree about how far money compensates for facial features.

angle.text: Money funds the looks-improving tools covered elsewhere in the wiki (skincare, hair, gym, surgery, clothing) and adds status, which proponents say raises how attractive someone is rated.

lead: Just be rich theory, abbreviated JBR, is a belief circulated on looksmaxxing forums that wealth outweighs or compensates for physical looks. A looksmax.org thread titled around JBR as the only non-'cope' ascension reflects the framing: income is presented as an alternative to being born with favoured facial traits.[1]

Believers argue that money improves appearance directly, by paying for skincare, dental work, hair treatments, fitness coaching, tailoring and cosmetic surgery, and indirectly, by raising status. Evolutionary-psychology accounts summarised on Wikipedia describe resources and status as attributes some people weigh in attraction, and note that height and body shape also act as status cues.[2]
No study has tested JBR as a formal theory. Related research on attractiveness examines how status, grooming and a halo effect shape how people are perceived.[2]
infobox: Wealth can override or offset facial looks

paras: The theory states that economic success is the most reliable way to improve one's standing in attraction and social treatment, whatever the starting face. It sits alongside other frameworks that rank paths to improvement.[1]

Proponents describe two channels. The first is purchasing: grooming, clothes, fitness, cosmetic dentistry, hair restoration and surgery all carry costs. The second is signalling: status and resources are thought to add to perceived attractiveness regardless of facial structure.[1]

Wikipedia's overview of physical attractiveness reports that attractiveness research links resources and status to attraction in some settings, that height can function as a status cue, and that one study reportedly found higher salary together with body proportions raised men's rated attractiveness.[2] It also describes the halo effect, in which attractive people are assumed to have positive traits.[2] These findings are general and do not test JBR itself.

lore.intro: The theory appears in looksmax.org discussions as an alternative to facial ascension.[1]
